title: King henry viii
summary: King Henry VIII is a Shakespearean history play, traditionally attributed in part to John Fletcher, dramatising the years roughly 1520 to 1533 at the court of Henry VIII of England. It opens with the fall of the Duke of Buckingham, who is arrested on treason charges engineered by the ambitious Cardinal Wolsey, and it moves on to the king's growing desire to annul his marriage to Queen Katharine of Aragon so he can wed Anne Bullen. Katharine's pleas before the cardinals, her dignified defence of her honour, and the sharp political intrigue among the nobles give the middle of the play its tension. Wolsey's downfall follows, and the play closes with the christening of the infant Princess Elizabeth, where Archbishop Cranmer delivers a prophecy praising her future reign. The play is written in blank verse with a prologue and epilogue, and it mixes court politics, pageantry, and personal grief. The excerpt provided covers the opening scenes, a central sequence involving Katharine and the cardinals, and the christening ending.
